title: Al-Wahid, the One
tomorrow: One, and Unique. why would the Qur'an need both words?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Maajid: the upper hand, and a neighbor's line, more blessed to give. The line: noble. Then a short question: Al-Wahid, the One. One what?

Some sentences are short enough to fit on a wristband and big enough to hold a whole faith. La ilaha illallah: there is no god but Allah. It's the first half of the shahada, the declaration of faith, and a hadith hopes it will be a person's last words too. So, one what? Not one of a set, like the best player on a team. Not one at the top of a ladder of gods. One with no second.
screen: `SHORT ENOUGH FOR A WRISTBAND.` → `NO GOD BUT ALLAH.` → `ONE WITH NO SECOND.`

segments.voice: In Pickthall's words: "Your God is One God; there is no God save Him, the Beneficent, the Merciful." Notice what comes right after the oneness: mercy. The One isn't cold or distant in that verse. And here's the detail worth telling a friend tonight. The same word family turns up in Surah an-Nisa, about people this time: "O mankind! Be careful of your duty to your Lord Who created you from a single soul." Single there is wahida, from the same word as today's Name. One God, and the whole human family traced back to one soul. That verse speaks to all mankind, not to one group. Now the week, looking back. Life is his: Abraham's birds and the rain. Death is his: we are Allah's and returning. Ever-living: tears and steadiness together. He holds it up: the One on the night shift. Lacking nothing: the found become finders. Noble: the upper hand. And today, one. That closes a long stretch of the Names, which began with Al-Ghafur, the one who covers faults.
screen: `YOUR GOD IS ONE GOD.` · `ONE, THEN MERCY.` · `FROM A SINGLE SOUL.` · `SIX LINES, ONE WEEK.` · then, large: `ONE.`

segments.voice: Say la ilaha illallah slowly, out loud or in a whisper, letting the breath carry it: la ilaha on one out-breath, illallah on the next. If the words aren't yours, keep the other half of the lesson instead: every person you'll pass today, traced back to one single soul. Keep that rhythm for the two minutes.
screen: `LA ILAHA, ON ONE BREATH.` · `ILLALLAH, ON THE NEXT.`

segments.voice: Al-Wahid. The One: One with no second, merciful in the very next breath, and the reason every soul traces back to one.
Last line of the stretch: one, one God and one human family from a single soul. Day fifteen-forty, whole.

fork.setup: at lunch someone says, 'your people, my people, totally different.' your friend wants a verse that speaks to everyone, not just Muslims. which one from today fits?
